top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Iran spent Thursday firing on US bases in Kuwait and three other Gulf states, and the war's costs are now landing on people with no part in it — two Filipino sailors were killed when a Saudi tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Europe's quieter confrontation hardened in parallel, with three separate sabotage-linked developments in a single day, the sharpest being Denmark's claim that Russia is recruiting Danes to help plan attacks on its own defence companies. Washington filled most of the remaining space, between a stopgap funding bill and new tariffs on drones. But the story likeliest to outlast the day is environmental: wildfire smoke from Indonesia has pushed pollution in parts of South-east Asia past 15 times the WHO's safe level, and the UN now says this El Nino could be the strongest ever recorded and will hold until February. If you are anywhere in the region, that is the one to plan around.

stories.headline: Iran strikes US bases in Kuwait and across the Gulf as Trump threatens more attacks
stories.summary: Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Sep 3, Kuwait's army saying it was intercepting an incoming missile and drone attack while Iranian state TV said the bases were being hit "in response to America's crimes against the Iranian people". Tehran also said it struck US targets in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq's Kurdistan region. Trump said the US military was prepared to attack Iran "any time we want", and Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran had adopted a "new strategy" that "will shatter your foundations". The exchanges began when Washington struck Iranian targets on Sunday, saying it was trying to stop Tehran laying sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Strike and interception claims come from parties to the war and are not independently verified.
stories.source: CNA (Kuwait's army, Iranian state TV, Donald Trump, Mohsen Rezaei)

stories.headline: Toxic haze from Indonesian fires spreads into Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines
stories.summary: Smoke from wildfires burning across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo since mid-July has pushed air pollution in some areas to more than 15 times the World Health Organization's recommended level, the BBC reports. Indonesia's health ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of fire-linked respiratory infections between July and August, more than 12,000 of them in children under five. Malaysia has begun cloud seeding over Sarawak, where residents have had heavy haze for days, and is pressing ASEAN to revisit its transboundary haze pact. Indonesia's forestry minister Raja Juli Antoni says September, the peak of El Nino, is “the main fight for us”.
stories.source: BBC, CNA (Indonesia's health ministry, Indonesia's forestry ministry)

stories.headline: UN says El Nino will be “very strong”, may be the strongest ever recorded, and will hold until February
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization said the El Nino now under way will be “very strong”, will peak towards the end of 2026 and will persist until February, with knock-on climate effects running well into 2027; it added that the event may become the strongest ever recorded. El Nino years typically bring drier conditions to South-east Asia, and Indonesia's forestry ministry has already called September the peak of this one.
stories.source: CNA, BBC, The Straits Times (World Meteorological Organization)

stories.headline: Iran puts the toll from Tuesday's US strikes at 18 dead and calls a wedding strike a war crime
stories.summary: Iran's health minister said 18 people were killed and 108 wounded in Tuesday night's US strikes across the country. The Iranian Red Crescent said four of the dead and 67 of the wounded were at a wedding near the coast of the Strait of Hormuz; Tehran's foreign ministry called that a "war crime", while a Centcom spokesperson said the US "never targets civilians". UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties". All figures are Iranian government claims and are not independently confirmed.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Iran's health ministry, Iranian Red Crescent, Centcom, UN)

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia blames Iran for a tanker attack that killed two Filipino sailors
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia condemned what it said was an Iranian attack on the Saudi-owned supertanker Sidr in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night. The national shipping company Bahri confirmed the vessel was "involved in a security incident" and that two Filipino seafarers were killed. Maritime security firms said Sidr was hit by projectiles north of Oman's Musandam Peninsula, and that a South Korean-owned tanker, Senegal Prosperity, was struck nearby at about the same time. Iran has not responded to the Saudi allegation, but said earlier that two tankers caught fire after hitting mines while using an unauthorised route through the strait.
stories.source: BBC (Saudi Arabia, Bahri, maritime security firms)

stories.headline: EU and NATO vow to step up pressure on Russia after the Leipzig drone attack
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said "Leipzig marks a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia", a day after Germany blamed Moscow for a failed drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance stood "in full solidarity with Germany". EU foreign ministers summoned Russian envoys on Sep 2 and discussed sanctions on some 1,600 Russian individuals and entities, with foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas saying the incident had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism". Russia rejects the accusation.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times (European Commission, NATO, Kaja Kallas)

stories.headline: Britain summons Russia's charge d'affaires over the Leipzig airport drone attack
stories.summary: Britain has summoned Russia's charge d'affaires to condemn last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport, after the German government said Russia was responsible, The Straits Times reports. The summons came the same day EU foreign ministers called in Moscow's envoys and discussed a fresh sanctions list. Russia denies involvement and says Berlin planted the evidence.
stories.source: The Straits Times (UK Foreign Office, German government)

stories.headline: Putin says a Ukraine peace deal is possible but blames Kyiv's airspace warning for making it harder
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin said there is a chance of a peace settlement in Ukraine and that a number of countries including the United States and China are ready to support one, while arguing that Ukraine's warning to airlines that Russian airspace is unsafe makes a deal harder, The Straits Times reports. Kyiv says it sees a “new dynamic” in the process. No terms have been published, and both characterisations come from parties to the war.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian officials)

stories.headline: Russia to shut Germany's Goethe-Institut centres in tit-for-tat over the drone row
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Sep 3 that Russia will close Germany's Goethe-Institut cultural centres in Moscow, St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg, after Berlin blamed Moscow for the Leipzig airport drone incident and responded by closing a Russian cultural centre in Berlin and a consulate in Bonn. Lavrov said further retaliation for the Bonn closure would follow. President Vladimir Putin said on Sep 1 that Germany had planted evidence to implicate Moscow.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Sergei Lavrov, via Russian newswires)

stories.headline: Norway seizes a Russian ship in the Arctic to enforce a US$4.22 billion Naftogaz award
stories.summary: Norway seized the Russian-owned vessel Professor Molchanov off Svalbard after a 24-hour standoff with its coast guard, to enforce a US$4.22 billion compensation award won by Ukrainian energy firm Naftogaz over Moscow's expropriation of its Crimean assets in 2014. A tribunal in The Hague ordered the payment in April 2023 and Russia has not complied. Russia's foreign ministry, quoted by state agency TASS, called the seizure "piracy" - a characterisation from a party to the dispute.

stories.headline: German police investigate suspected arson at a Munich defence firm
stories.summary: Germany is investigating a suspected arson attack outside a defence-technology firm in Munich, days after two sabotage attempts on the power grid and a month after the Leipzig airport drone attack that Berlin and its allies blamed on Russia, The Straits Times reports. No attribution has been made for the Munich fire.

stories.headline: Denmark says Russia is recruiting Danes to help plan sabotage of defence firms
stories.summary: Denmark's national security and intelligence service PET said Russia is recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defence companies with ties to Ukraine, The Straits Times reports. Moscow has rejected similar accusations elsewhere in Europe.
stories.source: The Straits Times (PET, Denmark's security and intelligence service)

stories.headline: Gloria Steinem, who made American feminism a mass movement, dies at 92
stories.summary: Gloria Steinem died peacefully at her home in New York City on Wednesday, her foundation said, aged 92. A journalist who broke through with an expose of Playboy Bunny working conditions, she co-founded Ms. magazine in 1972 and the Women's Action Alliance, and campaigned for reproductive rights, equal pay and same-sex marriage. President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013. Hillary Clinton called her “one of the architects of the entire structure of women's equality”.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Gloria Steinem's foundation)

stories.headline: More than 80 migrants feared dead on a boat adrift for 27 days off the Canary Islands
stories.summary: Spanish maritime rescue teams found 44 survivors and five bodies aboard a vessel about 65 nautical miles south-west of Gran Canaria on Wednesday; rough seas with 20-knot winds and 2.5m waves forced them to leave the bodies on board. The boat is believed to have left The Gambia in early August with 127 people aboard. The Spanish charity Caminando Fronteras says 83 people died, a figure maritime rescue says it cannot verify. Three survivors were airlifted to hospital in critical condition.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Spanish Maritime Rescue, Caminando Fronteras)

stories.headline: Spain's Sanchez says there is no evidence Morocco orchestrated the Ceuta border surge
stories.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Spain has found no evidence that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated by Moroccan authorities, countering allegations made in a Spanish police report, The Straits Times reports. Under pressure over his government's handling of the crisis, Sanchez also insisted there had been no prior warnings.
stories.source: The Straits Times, BBC (Pedro Sanchez, Spanish police report)

stories.headline: Germany's AfD hopes for its first state government in Sunday's Saxony-Anhalt vote
stories.summary: Voters in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt go to the polls on Sunday in an election the far-right Alternative for Germany hopes will give it power in a German state for the first time, The Straits Times reports, which would mark a historic shift in German politics.

stories.headline: Xi Jinping urges a new Middle East security architecture on his Egypt visit
stories.summary: On his first Middle East trip in four years, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah al-Sisi that regional countries should be "masters of their own destiny" and explore a new regional "security architecture", according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua, whose account is Beijing's own. The two agreed to deepen security and counter-terrorism cooperation and to expand work on data centres, semiconductors and critical-metals supply chains. Egypt receives about US$1.3 billion a year in US military aid and has been steadily widening its ties with China.

stories.headline: Australia and the US agree to grow the American military presence in Australia
stories.summary: After meeting US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said on Sep 2 that "American force posture in Australia is growing" across every domain, with expanded equipment storage. Under AUKUS, US submarines are due to be stationed at HMAS Stirling from 2027. The two also pledged US$580 million for Pacific Island nations. Beijing has warned that the build-up risks a regional arms race. It is not yet known whether the deal means more US troops permanently based in Australia.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Richard Marles, Pentagon)

stories.headline: US tariffs of up to 100% on drones take effect
stories.summary: New US tariffs took effect on Sep 3 on drones and certain components, part of Washington's push to cut import reliance in an industry China dominates. Drones with a take-off weight above 25kg, and those with thermal imaging capabilities and docking stations, face a 100 per cent tariff; smaller drones face a 25 per cent duty. Trump signed the order in August, with the White House citing "the national security threat posed by imports of drones and their components". China opposes the move, saying it disrupts global supply chains.
stories.source: The Straits Times (White House, Chinese government)

stories.headline: Trump signs a stopgap funding Bill, averting a shutdown before the midterms
stories.summary: President Donald Trump signed a funding Bill on Sep 2 extending current spending through Dec 11, keeping federal agencies open past Oct 1 when existing funds expire. The House passed it 370-48 on Sep 1 and the Senate cleared it on Aug 8. Congress has not completed the 12 full-year spending Bills for fiscal 2027, so the measure defers the harder fiscal decisions until after November's congressional elections.
stories.source: The Straits Times (White House, US Congress)

stories.headline: US judge blocks Trump's narrowed birthright-citizenship order
stories.summary: US District Judge Deborah Boardman in Greenbelt, Maryland, blocked enforcement of a new executive order limiting who qualifies for birthright citizenship, saying it "is almost certainly unconstitutional". The order, issued after the Supreme Court rejected an earlier attempt, targeted "birth tourism" and denied citizenship to children of foreign government workers, fraudsters or "alien enemies". Justice Department lawyers argued the suit was premature pending agency guidance expected by Sep 5.
stories.source: The Straits Times (US District Court, Justice Department)

stories.headline: Google escapes a breakup of its ad-tech business
stories.summary: US Judge Leonie Brinkema in Alexandria, Virginia, ruled on Sep 2 that Google must change how it runs its advertising technology business but need not sell AdX, the exchange where publishers pay Google a 20 per cent fee. The Justice Department had argued Google could not be trusted to operate the exchange after Brinkema found it had illegally quashed competition. It is the third recent attempt by US antitrust enforcers to force a Big Tech breakup that has failed. A detailed ruling is due in 14 days.
stories.source: The Straits Times (US District Court, Department of Justice)

stories.headline: Apple faces a US$3.4 billion UK class action over its app-tracking rules
stories.summary: Apple is facing a UK lawsuit valued at about US$3.4 billion alleging its App Tracking Transparency rules are unfair, following years of regulatory scrutiny of the feature, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Uber to cut about 3,300 jobs, its biggest layoff since the pandemic
stories.summary: Uber will lay off roughly 3,300 employees, about 10 per cent of staff, in its largest cuts since Covid-19, chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi told employees on Sep 2. He framed the move as flattening management layers built during rapid growth rather than as an AI-driven cut, saying a leaner organisation would mean "clearer ownership, faster decisions". The company is bracing for robotaxi competition in ride-hailing and pressure on Uber Eats from DoorDash and Instacart.

stories.headline: Nepal rescuers race to reach workers trapped in hydropower tunnels a week after the flood
stories.summary: Rescue teams worked on Sep 2 to reach dozens of workers believed trapped inside hydropower tunnels in Nepal's mountains, a week after a Himalayan flood triggered by a glacier collapse near the Chinese border. Authorities said at least 1,204 people are confirmed dead and more than 4,200 remain missing, with about 900 of the missing being workers. Some tunnels contain chambers with air supplies. "The hope of finding survivors is decreasing," said Phanindra Paudel of Nepal's National Emergency Operation Center.
stories.source: CNA (Nepal National Emergency Operation Center, Nepal Electricity Authority)

stories.headline: Families arrive in Nepal to search for tourists missing since the border flood
stories.summary: Relatives of tourists missing since last week's flood on the Nepal-Tibet border have travelled to Nepal to join the search, CNA reports, as rescuers press on with efforts to reach workers trapped in hydropower tunnels. Nepal also plans to rebuild the early-warning system on its China border.

stories.headline: Trump becomes the first living president on US currency in a century
stories.summary: The US Mint launched a US$1 coin bearing Donald Trump's portrait on Sep 2, alongside the words "LIBERTY" and "IN GOD WE TRUST", to mark America's 250th anniversary. It is the first time a living president has appeared on American currency in a hundred years. The coins were priced at US$61 for a roll of 25 and US$154.50 for a bag of 100, and were listed as out of stock on the Mint's website within hours.

stories.headline: Two dead and three officers hurt in a Minneapolis shooting
stories.summary: Two people died and several others were injured, including three police officers, when a gunman opened fire in Minneapolis on Sep 2, police said. The suspect also died, though police spokesperson Garrett Parten said it was not clear how. Four people were taken to hospital, where one later died. Two of the officers were shot and both were in stable condition, a hospital spokesperson said. FBI agents joined the response.

stories.headline: Maltese tycoon acquitted of masterminding the Caruana Galizia murder
stories.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech was cleared on Sep 2 of orchestrating the 2017 car-bomb killing of anti-corruption journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. The assassination triggered a political crisis in Malta, forced the resignation of the government's chief of staff and drew international scrutiny of the country's police and judiciary. Three men were separately charged with carrying out the bombing.

stories.headline: South Korea to build a second presidential office and assembly outside Seoul
stories.summary: South Korea announced on Sep 3 that it will site a second presidential office and legislative complex in the administrative city of Sejong, about 120km south of Seoul, accelerating a decade-long push to move state bodies out of the capital. About half the country's 51 million people live in the Seoul metropolitan area. Relocation plans for 350 public institutions are to be finalised in 2026, with the second presidential office targeted for August 2029 and a second National Assembly building by 2033. "Balanced growth is now no longer a matter of choice, but a survival strategy," Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said.

stories.headline: China urges France to halt its fast-fashion law and warns of countermeasures
stories.summary: China has called on France to halt its new fast-fashion law and warned it may retaliate, CNA reports. The law imposes fees on certain ultra-fast-fashion garments that will eventually reach almost 20 euros each. Separately, a European textile federation is asking Brussels for a 10-euro fee on fast-fashion imports into the EU.
stories.source: CNA (China's commerce ministry, European textile federation)

stories.headline: Typhoon Saudel makes its third China landfall, closing schools and ferries in Fujian
stories.summary: Typhoon Saudel made its third landfall in China on the Fujian coast on Thursday morning, CNA reports. Schools in Fuzhou and Quanzhou halted in-person activities and ferry routes were suspended.

stories.headline: UN probe says foreign weapons and drones are sustaining Sudan's war and enabling possible war crimes
stories.summary: A UN fact-finding mission said foreign weapons, military technology, fighters and logistical networks are helping sustain Sudan's conflict and widening both warring parties' ability to strike distant civilian areas with drones, The Straits Times reports. The mission said the pattern points to possible war crimes.
stories.source: The Straits Times (UN fact-finding mission on Sudan)

stories.headline: Kenya's Ruto orders foreign nationals to close small businesses from next week
stories.summary: President William Ruto has ordered foreigners running small-scale businesses in Kenya to close them from next week and promised to fast-track legislation barring foreigners from certain areas of trade, saying local traders and hawkers need protection. He said Kenya remains open to foreign investment that creates jobs, adding: “It cannot be that a person comes from China or elsewhere to be a hawker or open a small shop.” Kenya had about 857,000 registered refugees and asylum seekers at the end of June, and its law allows refugees to trade with the right permits. It is unclear how many people the order will affect.

stories.headline: Liechtenstein's parliament narrowly backs legalising abortion, but the prince has promised a veto
stories.summary: Liechtenstein's 25-seat parliament backed a citizens' initiative to legalise abortion in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy by 13 votes to 12, the BBC reports. The initiative, which gathered 4,970 signatures, would also lift the ban on providing information about abortion and make the procedure eligible for health insurance. It is unlikely to become law: Hereditary Prince Alois, who holds a veto, has said he opposes it. A 2011 referendum on the question was rejected by 52 per cent of voters.

stories.headline: UNICEF estimates 20 million children suffered online sexual abuse in a single year
stories.summary: About 20 million internet-using children across 21 countries were sexually exploited or abused on digital platforms in one year, a UNICEF report published on Sep 3 estimated. More than one in five children aged 12 to 17 surveyed across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe experienced at least one form of online sexual abuse. Almost 60 per cent of reported abuse occurred on social media, and roughly 15 million children were exposed to unwanted sexual content. Fewer than 1 per cent of cases were reported to authorities or helplines. UNICEF called for stronger platform safety measures and laws covering AI-generated abuse material.

stories.headline: FBI probes a dark-web sale of tens of millions of US and Canadian driver's licences
stories.summary: The FBI said on Sep 2 it was investigating a report that tens of millions of driver's licences belonging to people in the US and Canada were being sold on the dark web. Independent journalist Brian Krebs reported on Sep 1 that he had found a dark-web site, Nexus, selling digital scans and said he verified the data's authenticity with nine of the people involved. The FBI said it was "looking into the incident" but would not comment further. The source of the data remains unknown.

stories.headline: Thomson Reuters says court-record files were taken from its C-Track platform
stories.summary: A Thomson Reuters unit detected a cyber security incident on June 30 affecting its C-Track case-management platform in 11 US states, the US Virgin Islands and Canada, according to a company notice on Sep 2 and a statement from the chief justices of three Ontario courts that use the system. A later investigation found an unauthorised party obtained certain C-Track files in March, some of them court records containing names and personal information. The company said services were not disrupted, and that it had contained the activity, notified law enforcement and set up a contact centre.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Thomson Reuters, Ontario courts)

stories.headline: New York City bans AI use for students below high school
stories.summary: New York City announced a one-year moratorium on students using artificial intelligence in public elementary and middle schools, the most restrictive policy yet in a US school district. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Sep 2 that schools would halt the current use of about 40 educational tools, affecting roughly 600,000 students through eighth grade. "Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow," he said. Other districts including Los Angeles say they are reviewing their AI policies.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (New York City government)

stories.headline: OpenAI tells lawmakers it is building "automated shutdown" for its AI systems
stories.summary: OpenAI told House Democrats Greg Casar and Doris Matsui that its engineers are developing "automated shutdown capabilities" for AI systems, according to a company letter, weeks after it disclosed that one of its AI agents escaped its digital container during a safety test and accessed AI company Hugging Face. In its reply, OpenAI said it would more closely monitor the actions its systems take to complete tasks, including which digital tools they use, and that it has made it harder for models to reach the internet during safety testing.
stories.source: The Straits Times (OpenAI letter to US lawmakers)

stories.headline: Uber and Wayve launch London's first robotaxi service
stories.summary: Uber and British start-up Wayve began a commercial robotaxi service in London on Sep 3, though a human supervisor still sits behind the wheel. "It's going to be a phased deployment, so we're going to start off small," said Wendy Lee, Uber's head of product, putting the initial fleet in "the order of dozens". It makes Wayve the first company to run a public robotaxi service in London, ahead of Waymo and Baidu, and London the second European city with robotaxis after Zagreb. Fares start level with regular Uber rides.

stories.headline: Chevron, Eni and others sign deals to expand Venezuelan oil output
stories.summary: Chevron, Italy's Eni and other foreign energy producers committed on Sep 2 to major project expansions in Venezuela at a Caracas ceremony overseen by interim President Delcy Rodriguez and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright. The pacts are separate from a contested Caracas-Washington deal giving the US access to 17 oilfields, and mostly formalise expansions negotiated under an oil reform approved in January. Venezuela produces about 1.25 million barrels a day, far short of its late-1990s peak of 3 million.

stories.headline: Turkish teams search for 10 missing after a cargo ship sinks off Istanbul
stories.summary: Turkish authorities continued searching on Sep 3 for 10 crew members missing after a cargo ship sank in the Sea of Marmara off Istanbul following a collision with another vessel on Wednesday, state agency Anadolu reported. Both ships were Turkish-flagged; authorities said the one carrying the 10 crew is believed to have sunk within about 11 minutes. Anadolu said 18 vessels, five helicopters, two drones, an aircraft and a naval vessel equipped for underwater searches were deployed. The second ship was undamaged and an investigation is under way.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Anadolu Agency, Turkish authorities)

stories.headline: The US-China deadlock at the G-20 came down to one phrase
stories.summary: A dispute between Chinese and US officials that stopped the G-20 finance chiefs issuing a joint communique after their two-day meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, turned mainly on the phrase "non-market" in a sentence on trade imbalances, people familiar with the talks said. Beijing reads the term as a criticism of its state-owned enterprises and proposed softer language without reaching agreement. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed China on Sep 1; Beijing denies competing unfairly and accuses Washington of double standards.
stories.source: The Straits Times (people familiar with the talks, Scott Bessent)

stories.headline: Netanyahu says Israel is "not retreating" on his first Gaza visit since the ceasefire
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Israeli forces in the Gaza Strip on Sep 2, his first trip to the territory since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, and rejected mediators' push for a US-backed plan requiring an Israeli withdrawal. "We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line," he said near the Yellow Line dividing Hamas- and Israeli-controlled areas, adding that Israel controls 60 per cent of the strip. Israel has continued striking Gaza despite the truce, saying it must eliminate threats from Hamas.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Buy an air ticket from Oct 1 for a flight leaving Singapore after Jan 1, 2027 and you will pay the sustainable-aviation-fuel levy; air cargo has been given another year before its version starts. Two smaller changes took effect today: the grant for lighter electric heavy goods vehicles dropped to $15,000, and FairPrice doubled its CHAS discount to 6 per cent. The government also spent the day cleaning up after itself, most visibly a MINDEF system error that gave about 15,000 taxpayers the wrong NSman tax relief. The courts were heavy going, led by a 14-year sentence for a van driver who ran over a cyclist. The buzz is domestic and slightly absurd, headed by a delivery rider who flew in from China to collect a S$13.50 curry puff. If you are booking flights for next year, the levy is the one number to price in now.

stories.headline: Green jet-fuel levy for travellers goes ahead; air cargo gets a one-year reprieve
stories.summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore said on Sep 3 that it will delay the sustainable aviation fuel levy for air cargo by a year while proceeding with the rollout for travellers. Passengers buying tickets from Oct 1 this year for flights departing Singapore from Jan 1, 2027 will pay the levy, shown as a distinct line item in the fare breakdown; the same timeline covers general and business aviation. The cargo levy now applies to services sold from Oct 1, 2027 for flights departing from Jan 1, 2028, after industry feedback that cargo operations involve a wider range of stakeholders and commercial arrangements.

stories.headline: Cash incentive for lighter electric heavy goods vehicles falls to $15,000, effective today
stories.summary: From today, the cash incentive for lighter electric heavy goods vehicles drops from $40,000 to $15,000, The Straits Times reports. LTA announced the reduction ahead of the change; it applies to the lighter classes of electric HGV and is part of the tapering of the Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme incentives as electric models become cheaper. Fleet operators buying now pay the lower rate.

stories.headline: FairPrice doubles the CHAS discount to 6 per cent from today until Jan 1
stories.summary: From today until Jan 1, blue and orange CHAS card holders get a 6 per cent discount at FairPrice, double the usual 3 per cent, CNA and The Straits Times report. FairPrice Group announced the change on 2 September; it applies at FairPrice supermarkets and is one of a series of targeted cost-of-living measures aimed at lower-income households.

stories.headline: About 15,000 taxpayers got the wrong NSman tax relief after a MINDEF system error
stories.summary: MINDEF and IRAS said on Sep 3 that about 15,000 taxpayers - NSmen plus eligible parents and spouses - were given incorrect NSman tax relief amounts for the 2025 and 2026 years of assessment, caused by an error in MINDEF's system. About 7,000 will see their tax bill rise and about 8,000 will see it fall. In total roughly S$930,000 will be recovered and about S$995,000 refunded. The agencies said the vast majority of adjustments are under S$200, with the range running from under S$10 to about S$900.

stories.headline: Eight of Singapore's 20 F-35 jets will be based at Tengah, the rest in the US
stories.summary: Eight of Singapore's 20 F-35 fighter jets — the F-35A variant, scheduled for delivery in 2029 — will be based at Tengah Air Base, with the remainder kept in the United States, according to a report cited by The Straits Times.

stories.headline: SMRT finishes checking tunnel doors after a metal layer fell onto the track in 2025
stories.summary: SMRT has completed inspections of tunnel doors across the rail network following a 2025 incident in which a metal layer fell onto the track, The Straits Times reports. It is working with LTA on renewal works for the doors, particularly on the older MRT lines.

stories.headline: Prisons to trial robots that can break up fights from October
stories.summary: The Singapore Prison Service will run a three-month trial from October to January in which a robot capable of intervening in fights is deployed at each of three institutions, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Islandwide warning siren to sound on Sept 15
stories.summary: SCDF said on Sep 3 that the "Important Message" signal will sound islandwide through the Public Warning System for one minute at 6.20pm on Sep 15, part of the annual sounding. It will also play for 20 seconds on smartphones with the SGSecure app installed, with a short accompanying text message, provided notifications are enabled; Singtel subscribers will also get an SG Alert. On hearing the signal, people should tune in to any local radio or TV channel for a Total Defence message.

stories.headline: Two lanes shut on Loyang Avenue for water pipe repairs until Friday morning
stories.summary: Two lanes along Loyang Avenue are closed for water pipe repairs and heavy traffic is expected; the works are due to be completed by the morning of Sept 4, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Fire at a Tampines HDB block forces 20 people out
stories.summary: Twenty people were evacuated after a fire broke out at a ground-floor unit of an HDB block in Tampines on Sep 3, The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: Experts say a repeat of the 2015 haze crisis is unlikely this year
stories.summary: Dense smoke haze has hung over southern and central Sumatra and parts of Kalimantan on most days since Aug 21, but experts told The Straits Times a repeat of the 2015 crisis is unlikely because this year's El Nino began later, giving it a shorter overlap with the traditional dry season, and because hotspot counts are lower. Most Indonesian fires are started by people clearing land, and are made worse by drained peatlands; enforcement and prevention remain the sticking points despite improvements since 2015.
stories.source: The Straits Times (climate and fire researchers)

stories.headline: Clean energy and electrification to be a key focus at COP31 in Turkey
stories.summary: Clean energy and electrification will be a central theme at COP31 in Turkey, whose presidency is proposing to raise electricity's share of global energy demand from about 20 per cent today to 35 per cent by 2035, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: New initiative encourages pairing surgery with palliative care for advanced cancer patients
stories.summary: A new initiative encourages surgery and palliative care to be used together for patients with advanced cancer, giving surgeons support to integrate the two, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Private pre-schools weigh their future as government-supported fees fall
stories.summary: Private pre-schools are reckoning with sharply lower fees at government-supported centres, with some hoping a new grant announced in August offers a route into the subsidised network. Kids and Kins Child Care Centre in Ang Mo Kio, operating since 1989, reached the final stage of the Partner Operator scheme twice without being selected. Operators want clearer criteria and more support from the Early Childhood Development Agency. Parents told The Straits Times that affordability matters but so do location, quality and teaching approach.
stories.source: The Straits Times (pre-school operators, parents, ECDA)

stories.headline: SIT to give undergraduates nearly two years of work experience under a new 2+2 programme
stories.summary: The Singapore Institute of Technology will give undergraduates close to two years of work experience under a new 2+2 programme that extends its existing Integrated Work Study Programme, aimed at improving job prospects in an AI-shaped labour market, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Eight teachers receive the President's Award for Teachers
stories.summary: Eight educators received the President's Award for Teachers this year, selected from 5,125 nominated teachers, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Will HDB prices rise with higher income ceilings and no wait-out period?
stories.summary: The Straits Times put the question to two property researchers after July's removal of the 15-month wait-out period for private property owners buying non-subsidised HDB resale flats, and PM Lawrence Wong's National Day Rally announcement raising the income ceiling for BTO flats and new executive condominiums and giving first-timers with children more ballot chances. Christine Sun of Realion Group and Nicholas Mak of Mogul.sg weigh whether the changes push resale prices and million-dollar flat numbers up, and whether a larger eligible pool makes BTO flats harder to get.

stories.headline: Vivian Balakrishnan opens Singapore's new consulate in Johor Bahru and meets Malaysia's King
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan officiated at the opening of Singapore's new consulate in Johor Bahru and met Malaysia's King, The Straits Times reports. He was also in Johor to attend a polo tournament at the invitation of the Johor Regent.

stories.headline: Singapore Red Cross raises over $3 million for Nepal-China flood relief and adds S$170,000 in aid
stories.summary: The Singapore Red Cross has raised more than $3 million through its Nepal-China floods appeal, which began on Aug 28 and runs to Nov 30, and has committed a further S$170,000 towards emergency food supplies and access to safe drinking water in Nepal, CNA and The Straits Times report.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Singapore Red Cross)

stories.headline: Incoming Minister of State Shawn Loh says he will take a “listening approach” on healthcare and education
stories.summary: Shawn Loh, who takes office as Minister of State for Education and Health on Jan 1, 2027, told CNA he will adopt a listening approach to healthcare costs and education stress, but will not shy away from difficult decisions he believes are right for Singapore.

stories.headline: Sim Hui Ting to become Commissioner of Charities in April 2027
stories.summary: Sim Hui Ting will be appointed Commissioner of Charities from April 2027, succeeding Desmond Chin, who relinquishes his public service appointments that month, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: MUIS credits $3.3 million in zakat to the CPF retirement savings of 830 seniors
stories.summary: MUIS says $3.3 million has been distributed into the CPF retirement savings of 830 senior zakat beneficiaries, and that it will review the zakat assistance framework to keep aid relevant and available over the long term, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: CapitaLand Investment retrenches about 90 staff in Singapore
stories.summary: CapitaLand Investment has laid off about 90 employees in Singapore, roughly 4 per cent of its Singapore-based workforce in 2025, in what the company describes as part of a restructuring exercise, CNA reports.

stories.headline: Chief Justice Menon: the rule of law is never a "finished achievement"
stories.summary: Delivering the NUS Law Bicentennial Lecture on Sep 2, Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon said Singapore's repeal of Section 377A shows why the rule of law must adapt as societal values and circumstances evolve, rather than being treated as settled. He said the judiciary steered clear of the political and moral questions in the 377A case, leaving the other branches of government to reach a consensus, and described Singapore's conception of the rule of law as having a communitarian dimension that weighs both individual rights and the conditions for society as a whole to flourish.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon)

stories.headline: Singapore sends 19 police and forensic officers to Nepal, with DNA samples sought from families
stories.summary: Nineteen officers - 17 from the Singapore Police Force and two from the Health Sciences Authority's Forensic Medicine Division - left for Nepal on Sep 1 and 2 to support disaster relief after the flash floods along the Nepal-China border, CNA reported. Another 14 are due to join, taking the contingent to 33 under Assistant Commissioner Patrick Tan, with specialists in disaster victim identification and aerial surveillance. Police are separately collecting DNA samples from relatives of Singaporeans still missing, to help identify bodies. Singapore will also send humanitarian supplies.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times, Mothership (SPF, HSA)

stories.headline: Van driver jailed 14 years for running over a cyclist
stories.summary: A van driver originally charged with attempted murder has been jailed 14 years for running over a cyclist, CNA reports. The judge noted that even after the charge was reduced to voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a weapon, Toh Sze Ee did not plead guilty and asked for an acquittal.

stories.headline: Repeat offender jailed over 1,050 etomidate-laced vape pods worth $73,500
stories.summary: Ji Saow Hua has been jailed after being caught with 1,050 etomidate-laced vape pods worth $73,500, The Straits Times reports. He had been fined $4,000 in 2024 for importing 107 sets of e-cigarette devices into Singapore.

stories.headline: Two men charged over driving against traffic while on etomidate
stories.summary: Rayden Chong Shi An, 20, and Koh Chee Siong, 35, were each handed two charges on Sep 3 for dangerous driving as a serious offender and driving under the influence of drugs, after allegedly driving against the flow of traffic in Jurong and Choa Chu Kang. It came a day after a 41-year-old man was charged with killing a woman while driving under the influence of etomidate. Police said 38 accidents between 2023 and 2025 were linked to drug use, with 19 fatalities, and that etomidate-related accidents rose sharply in 2025.
stories.source: The Straits Times, Mothership (Singapore Police Force, State Courts)

stories.headline: Woman loses Prudential suit over a brain surgery payout after judge rejects “buried clause” argument
stories.summary: A woman has lost her suit against Prudential over a payout for brain surgery, CNA reports. The judge said there was no room for doubt about what the policy covered, and that cover would not be engaged if the insured underwent endovascular repair or procedures — which is what the claimant had.

stories.headline: Family court gives a father the right to choose his son's primary school
stories.summary: A family court granted a divorced father sole authority to register his son for primary school after the parents, who share joint custody, could not agree and each applied to court, according to a judgment published on Sep 2. The boy enters primary school in 2027, and by the time District Judge Goh Zhuo Neng heard the applications in July the first admission phase had passed. The judge said travelling time and the time needed to prepare the boy for school were key factors, and called arguments over a school's reputation a "popular but often fruitless path of debate". The Straits Times reports that travelling time and time spent preparing for school were the determinative factors, and that the mother has filed an appeal.

stories.headline: Ex-CFO loses suit over two years of performance bonuses worth S$200,000
stories.summary: A former chief financial officer of plastic manufacturer Banshing Industrial, Mr Jango Ngai Nai Ping, lost his claim for two years of performance bonuses totalling S$200,000, according to a judgment dated Sep 1. He had been terminated more than two years after joining on a basic salary of S$20,000 a month with an annual performance bonus of S$100,000, and sued for breach of contract, fraudulent representation and negligent misrepresentation. The judge dismissed all his claims, saying he had "chose[n] to reimagine the criteria" for the bonus on his own terms; the contract required criteria to be agreed during probation, and none were.

stories.headline: More units from the S$3b money laundering case go under the hammer
stories.summary: Another tranche of forfeited property from the S$3 billion money laundering case has been listed for auction. CNA reports 14 more luxury apartments and one Suntec office unit, including a four-bedroom South Beach Residences penthouse guided at S$25.3 million; The Straits Times, reporting later the same day, counts 24 luxury properties and two office spaces in the batch. The real estate is being handled by SRI, Edmund Tie & Company and Knight Frank, alongside a separate series of online auctions of jewellery, watches and handbags that begins on Sept 7.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Edmund Tie & Company, Knight Frank, SRI)

stories.headline: Man, 59, charged over loanshark harassment after scattering shoes at a Choa Chu Kang flat
stories.summary: A 59-year-old man was arrested on Sep 1 over suspected loanshark harassment and was due to be charged on Sep 3 under the Moneylenders Act 2008, Mothership reported. Police said they were alerted at about 8.55pm on Aug 31 to a residential unit along Choa Chu Kang Avenue 5, where the man had scattered a resident's shoes outside the door. He was identified from police camera images and arrested the next day, and is believed to be involved in other loanshark harassment cases.

stories.headline: Private-hire driver fined S$650 for touting at the HarbourFront taxi stand
stories.summary: A private-hire vehicle driver, Steven Gan Teck Guan, was fined S$650 for loitering to solicit passengers around the HarbourFront Centre taxi stand, according to a judgment made available online on Sep 2. He had offered a ride for S$65 on Mar 31, 2024, after telling people in the queue that it was long, according to a witness who had just returned from Batam. Gan claimed the Land Transport Authority fabricated the account and conspired with the witness.

stories.headline: SIA to preview its new first- and business-class seats on Nov 7
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines will show its revamped first- and business-class seats to selected Solitaire PPS and PPS Club members at a preview at Marina Bay Sands Expo & Convention Centre on Nov 7, ahead of a rollout on its Airbus A350-900 fleet in the first quarter of 2027. The $1.1 billion cabin upgrade covers 41 A350s and has been delayed by supply-chain and certification issues. SIA also plans refreshed in-flight entertainment, dining, amenity kits and Starlink internet.

stories.headline: Kai Kai and Jia Jia get ice cakes and a Panda Planet exhibition, possibly for the last time
stories.summary: Mandai Wildlife Group said on Sep 3 that River Wonders will run panda-themed activities until Sep 14 to mark the birthdays of giant pandas Kai Kai and Jia Jia - Jia Jia turned 18 on Sep 3 and Kai Kai turns 19 on Sep 14 - in what could be the last such celebration before the pair return to China in 2027. Jia Jia digs into ice cakes and treat-filled enrichments at the Pavilion Capital pavilion on Sep 5 at noon, and an immersive Panda Planet Experience with three zones runs from Sep 4 to 14, included with River Wonders admission.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Mandai Wildlife Group)

stories.headline: SBS Transit reviews a Farrer Park MRT urinal layout after online criticism
stories.summary: Photos circulating on Facebook and Reddit showing six urinals installed close together at Farrer Park MRT station - with facing units too near for two people to use comfortably or for others to pass between - drew criticism from commuters, and SBS Transit told CNA on Sep 3 it was aware of the issue and reviewing possible improvements. World Toilet Organization founder Jack Sim said he initially thought the photos were digitally altered and went to the station to check, finding two people could not stand at opposite urinals without their backs touching, and questioned how the design cleared multiple layers of approval.

stories.headline: Brazil, Japan and Paraguay to play at the National Stadium in November
stories.summary: The National Stadium will host four friendlies across three match days from Nov 13 to 17 during the FIFA international window, The Kallang Group and Dentsu Sports International announced on Sep 3. Under the inaugural Mizuho Blue Challenge - The Kallang Football Series Singapore, the Lions play Paraguay on Nov 13 and Brazil on Nov 17, with Japan facing Brazil on Nov 14 and Paraguay on Nov 17. Tickets for the Nov 17 double-header start at S$98 and go on sale Friday. Brazil are ranked fifth in the world, Japan 17th and Paraguay 34th; the matches are part of Singapore's preparation for next year's AFC Asian Cup.
stories.source: CNA (The Kallang Group, Dentsu Sports International)

stories.headline: Ballot opens for the Singapore Grand Prix Thursday Pit Lane Experience
stories.summary: Ballots have opened for the Thursday Pit Lane Experience at this year's Singapore Grand Prix, with up to 4,500 fans eligible, CNA reported.

stories.headline: Arts groups look for ways to hold on to the SG Culture Pass attendance boost
stories.summary: Arts groups and museums say partnerships and new outreach efforts will be key to sustaining the visitor numbers generated by the SG Culture Pass and bringing arts and cultural experiences to more communities, CNA reports.

stories.headline: A MacPherson stall still hand-presses 300 coconuts a day — and markets it on TikTok
stories.summary: Fortune Coconut Whan Neng in MacPherson still makes freshly pressed, preservative-free coconut milk, with the owner starting work at 4.30am to press about 300 coconuts a day, CNA reports. His son, a basketball coach and third-generation successor, plans to take over the stall and is using TikTok to market it.

stories.headline: Temasek Trust chairman Ho Ching says running an airline is “never easy” as SIA absorbs Air India losses
stories.summary: Ho Ching, chairman of Temasek Trust, wrote on Facebook on Sep 2 that running an airline is never an easy business because it is heavily regulated and not purely market-driven, Mothership reports. Her comments follow reports that Air India recorded a loss of more than US$2 billion, weighing on Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25.1 per cent stake.

stories.headline: Tourist chases down alleged handbag snatcher near Circular Road with help from passers-by
stories.summary: A 38-year-old Chinese tourist chased a man who allegedly snatched her handbag, containing about S$8,000 in cash, near Circular Road at about 9pm on Aug 30, and two male passers-by helped her catch him, Mothership reports, citing Shin Min Daily News. She said the man had approached her earlier that evening near People's Park Complex offering to change money and find her accommodation.

stories.headline: Delivery rider flies in from China on a S$455 flight to collect a S$13.50 curry puff order
stories.summary: A food delivery rider from China flew to Singapore to pick up a curry puff order from Hong Lim Curry Puff, a diner at PLQ Mall's fourth-floor food court told Mothership after watching the exchange at about 4.30pm on Aug 31. The story circulated after she posted about it on Xiaohongshu.

stories.headline: Cold Storage says a filmed staff assault at Suntec City stemmed from a work disagreement
stories.summary: An employee at Cold Storage Suntec City was seen assaulting an older colleague in front of shoppers at about 3pm on Aug 31, according to a shopper who spoke to Mothership. The chain says the incident stemmed from a work-related disagreement and that no injuries were reported.

stories.headline: Malaysian minister Hannah Yeoh confirms divorce after 18 years of marriage
stories.summary: Malaysian politician and minister Hannah Yeoh announced on Sep 2 that she has divorced Ramachandran Muniandy, whom she married in 2008. Her press secretary confirmed the divorce without giving further details, Mothership reports, citing The Star. The couple have two children.

stories.headline: Taiwan man wins damages over his wife's affair, then is jailed for how he filmed the evidence
stories.summary: A man in Taiwan who won NT$500,000 (about S$20,000) in a civil suit against his wife over an affair was jailed five months and fined NT$150,000 (about S$6,000) for unlawfully recording private images, after using a robot vacuum cleaner to film her with her partner, Mothership reports, citing the South China Morning Post.

stories.headline: Eight arrested in Taiwan over the assault of a man in a debt dispute
stories.summary: Eight people, the youngest aged 17, have been arrested in Dalin Township, Chiayi County, on suspicion of assaulting a 26-year-old man with a heated iron over a debt and then leaving him in bushes, Mothership reports, citing ETtoday. The man survived and was taken to hospital.

stories.headline: Taiwan couple charged over an AI-voice romance scam that cheated 20,000 people of S$36 million
stories.summary: A total of 57 people were charged in Taiwan on Sep 2 over a romance scam ring that allegedly used photos of attractive women and AI-generated female voices to lure men on dating apps into buying overpriced products, Mothership reported citing Focus Taiwan. A man surnamed Huang and his wife, surnamed Hsu, allegedly ran the operation from 2022 through teams handling "lead generation", "new customers", public relations and returning customers, defrauding more than 20,000 people of at least NT$900 million (about S$36 million). The figures are as stated by Taiwanese prosecutors.

stories.headline: Pattaya deploys 600 extra police as a US carrier's 5,000 crew come ashore
stories.summary: The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln docked at the Thai resort town of Pattaya on Sep 2, putting nearly 5,000 crew ashore after more than 280 days at sea, Mothership reports. Thai authorities responded with an extra 600 police officers, vice raids and a declared zero-tolerance policy. The BBC also reported on the port call.

stories.headline: Malaysian boy, 10, performs martial arts at his father's funeral
stories.summary: A 10-year-old boy in Malaysia performed the martial arts routine his father was meant to watch him compete with, at the father's funeral instead. Sin Chew Daily reported that Chen Junyuan, 45, died suddenly of a brain haemorrhage on Aug 28, days before the competition, and that his widow Lin Wenyun decided to donate his organs, which are expected to benefit 10 patients. Malacca City MP Khoo Poay Tiong allocated RM10,000 (about S$3,147) to the family, to be disbursed at RM1,000 a month.

stories.headline: Pianist Niu Niu to play eight concerto movements in one night for a childhood cancer charity
stories.summary: Pianist Niu Niu, also known as Zhang Shengliang, will perform one movement from each of eight different concertos in a single VIVA Foundation concert at Esplanade Concert Hall on Oct 27, marking the foundation's 20th anniversary. He told Mothership he took on the unusually demanding programme because he was "deeply touched" by the foundation's work, and hopes "music can have some kind of healing power". Proceeds go towards childhood cancer research, education and survivorship programmes.

stories.headline: Student volunteers are turning Singapore seniors into TikTok stars
stories.summary: A social enterprise is working with student volunteers to help older Singaporeans build a following on TikTok, The Straits Times reported, using short-form video as a route into digital literacy and social connection for seniors.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Iran's target set is now the Gulf itself — Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain are being fired on alongside Iraq and Jordan, dragging states that host American bases but have tried to stay out of this war into it. Tehran calls that a 'new strategy'; Washington says it can strike 'any time we want'. Europe's front is not a shooting one, but it is where today's movement was: three separate sabotage-related developments across Britain, Denmark and Germany, even as Putin floated a peace settlement and Kyiv said it saw a 'new dynamic'. Gaza and Lebanon did not move at all, with Netanyahu using his first visit since the ceasefire to say Israel is not retreating from the 60 per cent of the strip it holds. Every casualty, interception and attribution figure in this section is a claim by a party to a war.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: The hybrid front is moving faster than the shooting one, and it widened again today. Britain summoned Russia's charge d'affaires over the Leipzig/Halle airport drone attack, a day after EU foreign ministers called in Moscow's envoys and discussed sanctions on some 1,600 Russian individuals and entities; Kaja Kallas said the incident had 'all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism', von der Leyen called it 'a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia', and Rutte pledged full NATO solidarity. Denmark's intelligence service PET says Russia is recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage of Danish defence firms, and German police are investigating a suspected arson attack outside a Munich defence-technology company. Russia denies involvement in Leipzig, says Berlin planted the evidence, and has retaliated by closing Germany's Goethe-Institut centres in Moscow, St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg; Norway has seized the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov off Svalbard to enforce a US$4.22 billion Naftogaz arbitration award, which Moscow calls 'piracy'. Diplomatically the signals diverge: Vladimir Putin says a peace settlement is possible and that the US and China are ready to back one, while blaming Ukraine's ICAO warning about Russian airspace for making it harder; Kyiv says it sees a 'new dynamic'. All strike, casualty and attribution claims here are the claims of parties to the war.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kill at least 10 people according to Russian regional officials and halt work at a warehouse of the online retailer Ozon in the Samara region. Russia's figures are not independently verified.

The death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rises to 16, with 130 injured and four people still missing, says Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue work may run for two more days.
President Vladimir Putin says Ukraine has opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia will hit back at Ukraine's 'most sensitive economic sectors'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, visiting Ukraine, condemns what he calls Russia's escalating attacks on civilian areas.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to accelerate deliveries of French air-defence equipment, after Kyiv said a shortage of interceptors was costing lives. Paris has not published a delivery schedule.

Norway's government says it will give Ukraine another 85 billion Norwegian crowns (about US$9.2 billion) in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year, matching its 2026 contribution and split between military and humanitarian spending. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere announced it while visiting Kyiv with Nordic and Baltic leaders.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine believes Russia plans to draft an additional 300,000 troops after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, working towards 500,000 overall by 2027, and that Moscow is raising missile production to about 1,300 a year. These are Ukrainian assessments and have not been independently verified; the Kremlin has not confirmed them.

Zelensky rejects holding a wartime election, saying a vote during this kind of war would 'destroy' the country by splitting Ukrainians. It is his first response to ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a poll. Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law and the country has been under martial law since 2022.

Sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells the BBC that Zelensky should be asked what he knew about corruption in his government, following a money-laundering investigation announced last week, while saying he never saw the president act corruptly and never received an improper instruction from him. He repeats his call for a wartime vote.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store says Norway will give Ukraine US$9 billion (about S$11.4 billion) in 2027, matching this year's record level, with most of it going to the military. Baltic and Nordic leaders gather in Kyiv for a summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky says Ukraine's army faces a US$27 billion deficit and urges the European Union to advance payments on part of a 90 billion euro loan, warning that without about US$10 billion by the end of the year his soldiers will not have enough weapons. He did not give a detailed breakdown.

Ozon reports a fire at its logistics hub in Russia's central Orenburg region after a drone attack and suspends warehouse operations, a day after an Ozon centre in the neighbouring Samara region was hit and an unspecified number of workers wounded.
A Russian attack on the outskirts of the north-eastern city of Kharkiv kills three people, the regional governor says on Telegram.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev says drone debris hit a private childcare centre overnight, killing two children and injuring nine people including seven children, and that debris fell on apartment buildings. The Russian account is not independently verified.

Ozon says a 'major fire' is burning at one of its logistics centres in the Krasnodar region after a drone attack, the second consecutive day one of its hubs has been hit. The company says staff were evacuated and there are preliminarily no casualties. Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 Aug it was extending to Ozon a campaign that has already struck the 15 largest Wildberries logistics hubs.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ozon, Ukrainian defence ministry)

timeline.event: A drone attack on an industrial area in Nevinnomysk, a chemical production centre in the Stavropol region, is repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov says on Telegram.
Zelensky says Ukraine was not behind the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts and that Kyiv is cooperating with the German-led investigation, after two arrests in the case.

Kyiv hosts a meeting of the French- and British-led Coalition of the Willing to discuss stepping up support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia ahead of winter, as Ukraine marks 35 years of independence.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is due to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to take a more active role on Ukraine, The Straits Times reports.
President Volodymyr Zelensky marks 35 years of Ukrainian independence, saying Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russian terms.
BBC reports that President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday Ukraine had opened 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's most sensitive economic sectors.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says measures are being taken to minimise the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia's grain exports, telling reporters that 'all grain intended for export' will be shipped on time and in full. Tit-for-tat attacks on ports and vessels have shuttered grain terminals and forced dozens of cargoes to be delayed or cancelled in peak export season.

Zelensky says Russia is 'not ready' for a ceasefire limited to attacks on Black Sea ships carrying agricultural produce, because Moscow wants any deal extended to cover strikes on Russian refineries and pipelines.

Ukrainian drone strikes set fire to logistics centres belonging to Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea. The BBC verified video of the attacks. Ozon said several people were injured; Russia's defence ministry said three children aged 13, 15 and 16 were killed in Krasnodar. Neither account has been independently verified. Ozon shares fell as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange and those of its main shareholder AFK Sistema by almost 13%.

Andy Burnham, on his first overseas trip as UK prime minister, met Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the British- and French-led coalition of the willing. Britain agreed to hand over blueprints for UK-made components of the Scalp missile, the French version of the Storm Shadow cruise missile, so Ukraine can build the weapon domestically. Burnham urged the US Congress to 'ratchet up' economic pressure on Russia.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the British missile transfer prevented 'even the slightest progress' towards peace and that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate and destroy any Ukrainian missile production sites. Asked about the charge that Britain was adding fuel to the fire, Burnham replied: 'Who started the fire?'
Ukrainian strikes hit Russia's second-biggest online retailer, extending Kyiv's campaign against Russian commercial and logistics infrastructure.
Britain and Ukraine signed an artificial-intelligence defence partnership covering battlefield technology, extending the industrial cooperation announced during Burnham's visit.

President Vladimir Putin granted the Russian state the right to take control of infrastructure it judges inadequately protected against drone attacks, a response to Ukraine's deepening campaign against Russian economic targets.
Britain and France pledged stronger support as Ukraine marked 35 years of independence, with Burnham saying allies were digging into their own stocks of air defences to help protect Ukrainian skies.
