Iran seizes a sugar-carrying bulk carrier that authorities say dumped burnt oil, bilge water and industrial sludge into the Strait of Hormuz, referring it to the judiciary. Hormozgan ports official Esmaeil Makizadeh gave no flag or crew nationality. Iran has demanded compensation for several recent oil spills and says it plans to charge transit fees to fund services including environmental protection — fees the United States fiercely opposes.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Hormozgan Ports and Maritime Department)

timeline.event: Oil settles more than 2.5 per cent higher on the resumption of fighting: Brent up US$2.39 to US$90.49 a barrel and WTI up 2.83 per cent to US$85.76, with Brent touching US$91.52 intraday, its highest since 25 August. Shipping data showed visible commodity vessels transiting Hormuz fell to five a day over the weekend, against about a fifth of global oil supply before the war. Mediation on reopening the strait has stalled.
timeline.source: CNA (ICE and NYMEX settlement data, shipping data)

timeline.event: Oil prices extend their gains and Asian equity markets fall on fears of renewed US-Iran military exchanges after the weekend flare-up and President Donald Trump's warning that he will hit Iran 'hard'. Tokyo, Hong Kong, Seoul, Shanghai, Sydney and Singapore all trade lower. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed by Tehran while Washington continues its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran's central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati says Iran has sufficient foreign currency reserves despite US sanctions and that the bank is ready to inject up to US$2 billion into the foreign exchange market to calm volatility, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. 'I am telling the President of the United States: Iran has (foreign) currency and it has enough,' he said. The remarks follow US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's claim that Tehran is lashing out because it is losing the economic war, and come after Iranian officials including President Masoud Pezeshkian pointed to growing economic difficulty. Hemmati's figures are the Iranian central bank's own and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Tasnim, Central Bank of Iran)

timeline.event: Iran says it will reciprocate if the United States honours its commitments under the June interim deal. A senior Iranian source describes the recent exchanges of fire as a “limited and contained confrontation” but says Tehran would respond harshly to any further attack; President Donald Trump, quoted by a Fox News reporter as saying “we're going to hit them hard”, separately told reporters the strikes did not signal a return to full-scale war. Neither account has been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian presidency, senior Iranian source, Fox News quoting Trump)

timeline.event: US Central Command says American forces resumed strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets from 12:00 US Eastern time on Tuesday, citing 'recent attempted attacks' by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Red Crescent says shrapnel from a US missile hit a house where a wedding was being held in Sirik in southern Iran, killing four people - Iranian state media says a four-year-old child was among them - and wounding more than 50. Iranian reports also describe projectiles hitting Chabahar, Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, with explosions heard on Qeshm island and in Bandar Abbas. Casualty and damage claims are from parties to the fighting and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA (US Central Command, Iranian Red Crescent, Iranian state media)

timeline.event: President Donald Trump, as the US strikes were announced, warns that Iran will be hit at 'a much harder and higher level' if it retaliates.

Iran launches a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Aqaba, Jordan, in retaliation for the Sirik strike, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, and attacks US bases in Iraq. The Jordanian Armed Forces say they intercepted 13 ballistic missiles, destroying 10, with three falling in remote areas and no deaths or injuries; Jordan's national security centre warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governorates about falling debris. Kuwait's army says its air defences responded to Iranian missile attacks, and Iranian state media report several explosions in Bahrain. The IRGC says the US will 'regret' the strikes.
timeline.source: BBC (Jordanian Armed Forces, Kuwaiti army, Tasnim, IRGC)

timeline.event: Oil settles more than US$4 a barrel higher on the renewed US-Iran fighting. Iran's parliament speaker urges Iranians to cut petrol use, and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington plans to increase economic sanctions on Iran and has discussed further action with allies as well as Russia and China.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (settlement data, Iranian parliament, US Treasury)

timeline.event: The United Nations faces a contentious vote on Iran's nuclear programme ahead of the General Assembly, The Straits Times reports.

The Iranian Red Crescent raises the toll from the US strike on Sirik, on the Strait of Hormuz, to five killed - including a child - and more than 50 injured, saying shrapnel from a US missile hit a house where a wedding was being held. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, for Centcom, says the US is aware of the reports and that 'the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC'.
timeline.source: BBC (Iranian Red Crescent, US Central Command)

timeline.event: The IRGC fires missiles and drones at US targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Iraq and Bahrain. Jordan's armed forces say they intercepted 13 ballistic missiles, destroying 10, with three falling in remote areas and no deaths or injuries; Kuwait's army says its air defences responded; Iranian state media report explosions in Bahrain and IRNA says the IRGC destroyed a maintenance centre, warehouses and equipment at US bases in Iraq's Kurdistan region. All figures are the claims of parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: BBC (Jordanian Armed Forces, Kuwait army, IRNA, Tasnim, IRGC)

timeline.event: Centcom says its latest wave of strikes on IRGC targets began at 12:00 US Eastern time and was completed by early Wednesday, citing recent attempted IRGC attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on American forces. Iranian state media report projectiles hit Chabahar, Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, with explosions heard on Qeshm island and in Bandar Abbas.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (US Central Command, Iranian state media)

timeline.event: Crude rises more than 2 per cent and is up about 10 per cent on the week, with the Strait of Hormuz - about a fifth of world oil and gas traffic - effectively closed. Bond yields hold at multi-decade highs, 30-year UK gilts at their highest since 1998, and traders price in roughly a 70 per cent chance of a US Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bloomberg.
timeline.source: CNA (ICE/NYMEX settlement data, Bloomberg, Gama Asset Management)

timeline.event: A car strikes a gathering of supporters of Iran's government and armed forces in the north-eastern city of Mashhad overnight, killing four people and injuring more than 10, several Iranian media report. The circumstances have not been independently confirmed.

Iran says at least 12 people were killed in the latest US strikes, five of them at a wedding at a home in Sirik on the coast of the Strait of Hormuz, including a four-year-old. Iranian media put the wounded there at as many as 68 and published images of injured children. The figures are Iranian official and state-linked accounts and are not independently verified.

Qatar, host of the largest US air base in the Gulf, says it holds Iran fully legally responsible for the attacks and their consequences; Bahrain, which houses the US Navy's regional headquarters, says Iranian drones were intercepted and destroyed.
Iran says two tankers were struck by mines while being steered across the Strait of Hormuz by US vessels through a channel Tehran says it has closed. The claim has not been independently confirmed.
Saudi shipping company Bahri says two of its sailors were killed in an incident involving one of its oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August.
Aides to President Donald Trump, worried about a midterm rout, are pressing to keep the Iran war 'quiet' for now, The Straits Times reports.
Iran urges the United States to comply with the interim deal after Trump threatens further strikes.

Iran's health minister says 18 people were killed and 108 injured in Tuesday's US strikes, revising up an earlier figure of at least 12. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei calls a strike that hit a wedding at a home in Sirik a 'war crime'; the Iranian Red Crescent says shrapnel killed four people there, including two children. A Centcom spokesperson says the US 'never targets civilians' and is aware of the reports. Iranian authorities say another 14 people were killed elsewhere. None of the figures are independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC (Iranian health ministry, Iranian Red Crescent Society, Esmaeil Baqaei, US Central Command)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia condemns what it says was an Iranian attack on the Bahri-owned supertanker Sidr in the Strait of Hormuz at about 23:40 local time on Monday. Bahri confirms two Filipino seafarers were killed. Maritime security firms say Sidr was hit by projectiles north of Oman's Musandam Peninsula and that the South Korean-owned Senegal Prosperity was struck east of Musandam around the same time. Iran has not responded to the allegation, but said earlier that two tankers caught fire after striking mines on an unauthorised route.
timeline.source: BBC (Saudi government, Bahri, maritime security firms)

timeline.event: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warns that operations against American forces in the region will continue until the US 'regrets' its actions.
Israel says it is prepared to 'respond with great force' if Iran attacks, with forces readied for a possible attack over the Jewish high holiday season beginning in mid-September.
President Donald Trump floats renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait', after claiming US sovereignty over the waterway Tehran has effectively shut for six months.

Iran attacks US military bases in Kuwait. Kuwait's army says it is intercepting a missile and drone attack; Iranian state TV says the strikes target US bases in the Gulf state 'in response to America's crimes against the Iranian people'. Tehran says it also hit US targets in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq's Kurdistan region. Trump says the US is prepared to attack Iran 'any time we want'; security chief Mohsen Rezaei says Iran has adopted a 'new strategy' that 'will shatter your foundations'. All strike and interception claims are from parties to the war.
timeline.source: CNA (Kuwait's army, Iranian state TV, Donald Trump, Mohsen Rezaei)

timeline.event: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres says he is 'deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties, including a strike that reportedly hit a wedding ceremony in Iran'.

On his first Middle East visit in four years, Chinese President Xi Jinping tells Egypt's Abdel Fattah al-Sisi that regional countries should be 'masters of their own destiny' and explore a new regional 'security architecture', according to Chinese state agency Xinhua. The two agree to deepen security and counter-terrorism cooperation. Egypt receives about US$1.3 billion a year in US military aid.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says Washington will expand sanctions on Iran's trade partners to choke its economy, as the US presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports while Tehran keeps its hold on the Strait of Hormuz.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Both ceasefires are being outlived by the violence they were meant to stop, and the diplomacy has stalled outright. Netanyahu made his first visit to Gaza since the October 2025 truce and rejected the mediators' push for withdrawal, saying 'we control the area, we are not retreating' and that Israel holds 60 per cent of the strip. Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory this year and over 1,300 since the 10 October truce, including 301 children; the UN treats the figures as reliable and BBC Verify's analysis is consistent with them, while the Israeli military disputes them. Violence has spread to the West Bank, where Palestinian officials say two teenagers were killed by settler militants and army troops. In Lebanon, Unifil says Israel has added bases inside the zone it invaded, and the Ali al-Taher ridge in the south has become the war's most contested ground. Casualty figures from parties to the conflict are claims, not verified facts.

timeline.event: A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

Israel says it fired at a 'terrorist' in southern Syria; Syria's foreign ministry says an Israeli drone hit a civilian car near Beit Jinn, west of Damascus, calling it a 'blatant violation' of Syrian sovereignty. Syrian state TV reports one person injured. It is the second Israeli strike in Syria in a week, after the Abu al-Duhur airbase attack the US called an 'unnecessary escalation'.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli military, Syrian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reports that the widening confrontation between Israel and Turkey could reshape the region, with Syria - which physically separates the two - bearing the brunt of their rivalry.

Syria's government condemns the Israeli strike on the village of Beit Jinn, south-west of Damascus, as a violation of its sovereignty and of international law; officials say it hit a civilian vehicle and injured several people. The Israeli military says it targeted a 'terrorist' in the 'final stages' of preparing attacks posing an immediate threat to its soldiers.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Syrian officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says the earlier Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase could be 'the Israelis baiting the Turks' in an attempt to draw Ankara into a conflict. Washington had already called that strike an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says he expects security talks with Israel to resume soon despite an absence of trust, with Damascus seeking an Israeli withdrawal from Syrian land and an end to strikes. He says the US is pressing Israel to return to negotiations, and denies Syria allowed Turkish forces at the airbase Israel bombed this week.

Syria and Israel hold high-level US-mediated talks in Jordan, focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement, Syria's state news agency SANA reports citing a diplomatic source. Israel's prime minister's office did not comment.

At the Jordan talks, Damascus says its immediate priorities remain an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on 8 Dec 2024 and full restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, and that it will not accept limits on rebuilding its armed forces, according to SANA.

Syrian state news agency SANA reports that Syria and Israel held further US-mediated talks aimed at easing tensions, following the round held in Jordan on 23 August. Israel's prime minister's office has not commented.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz warned of 'forceful actions' after four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, about 800m from the Gaza boundary, and several more elsewhere in southern Israel. The Israeli military said the kites carried no suspicious materials and posed no threat. Hamas denied responsibility, called them 'basically children's toys from displacement camps', and accused Israel of using them as a pretext for continued strikes despite the ceasefire agreed last October.
Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu. There was no Saudi confirmation of the claim.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli fire killed two young children. The account comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, and removed Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from its list of global terrorist organisations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it recognised Damascus distancing itself from international terrorism; Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called it a 'historic step'. Syria remains at the centre of tension between Israel and Turkey.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria 'shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past' after the US removed the country from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list, thanking President Trump. The Treasury announced corresponding sanctions relief; Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was also delisted as a global terrorist organisation.

Far-right Israeli lawmaker and settler activist Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in Madama in the northern occupied West Bank while under military escort. The army said the demolition was unauthorised and a misuse of security protection, that soldiers stopped it and removed him, and that it viewed the incident with 'utmost severity'; Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot also criticised him.

Parents in Gaza were urged to stop children flying kites after Israel's warning to Hamas over kites found near the boundary. Israel's defence minister had threatened 'forceful actions'; the Israeli military says the kites carried nothing dangerous and Hamas calls them children's toys.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli attacks killed five people including two children. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

An official on President Trump's US-led 'Board of Peace' said all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites, and added that 'Israel, too, must comply with the ceasefire' and that military action cannot extend beyond genuine and imminent threats. The UN and Hamas called the kite warnings outrageous.

Israeli forces took control of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training centre between Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and the Qalandia refugee camp. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the evacuation followed the law Israel passed severing ties with the agency; UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the raid. The centre, opened in 1952, trains about 340 West Bank Palestinians a year.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UNRWA, Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Syria's Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution as part of an agreed integration into the Damascus government's structures.
President Trump sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, while saying Riyadh must recognise Israel.
Israeli forces have taken control of a UN training centre for Palestinians, The Straits Times reports. UNRWA has not said whether courses there will continue.

Israel's seizure of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training college in East Jerusalem drew international condemnation. Israel's government says the site was evacuated lawfully; UNRWA disputes the basis for the takeover.
A far-right Israeli lawmaker damaged a Palestinian memorial with a sledgehammer, footage of the incident showed.
Lebanon accused Israel of setting fire to forest and farmland in the south of the country. Israel has not commented on the accusation.
US Senate Democrats urged Israel to rein in settler violence in the West Bank.
Turkey said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces would help Syrian unity, a day after the SDF announced it was integrating into Damascus government structures.

The United States designated the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation and imposed sanctions on it. The group has previously said its actions target arms manufacturing sites.
An Israeli court acquitted, on grounds of mental health, the man filmed on CCTV attacking a nun in Jerusalem.
A funeral was held in the West Bank for Sliman Mansour, one of the best-known Palestinian artists of his generation.

Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials in Gaza said. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's envoy for Gaza, criticised both Israeli strikes and Hamas's actions and warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be 'a point of no return' for the region.

The UN human rights office condemned the United States' designation of the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation, saying the label risks criminalising protest. The State Department announced the designation, with sanctions, on 26 August.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights)

timeline.event: A former British-Israeli hostage held by Hamas married in Tel Aviv, in one of the more visible personal milestones since last October's ceasefire.
An Israeli air strike killed a Hamas operative and two other people near Jenin in the occupied West Bank, the Israeli military said, in a rare use of air power in the territory.
The BBC published the results of a week spent tracking settler violence in the occupied West Bank, documenting incidents against Palestinian communities.

Druze factions blocked students from sitting examinations in a dispute with the Syrian government, The Straits Times reported, the latest friction between Damascus and communities in the south as the new government consolidates control.

Dozens of Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Qusra near Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, residents and the Israeli military say. A resident tells AFP a small group approached villagers working on a house, then returned with dozens more, surrounded them and threw stones. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the attack, a rare step; Israeli forces deploy to the site.

Israel's military says it struck a Hamas commander "hiding within the compound" of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, saying medical facilities must not be used for militant activity. Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes elsewhere in the territory killed four people. Both accounts are contested and not independently verified.
Druze factions in southern Syria block students from sitting state examinations in a dispute with the Damascus government, The Straits Times reports.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the settler attack on the West Bank village of Qusra, calling it a criminal act that does not represent Israeli society; the Israeli military says it has opened an investigation. Palestinian residents say the village had been under a supply blockade for weeks before the attack.

The Straits Times reports that killings of Palestinian children and teenagers by Israeli forces and settlers have risen sharply in the occupied West Bank this year. Israel says its forces operate against militants; the two accounts of individual incidents frequently diverge and are rarely independently adjudicated.

An Israeli air strike near a bakery in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza kills a man and a three-year-old boy and wounds several others, Gaza health officials say; the Israeli military says it attacked a Hamas militant. Gazan health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Both tallies come from parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: An AFP investigation reports that Israeli forces and settlers have killed Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank at an average of about seven a month since October 2023, against roughly one a month before. Families say Israeli military investigations rarely produce accountability; the Israeli military says it investigates such deaths.
Israel's far-right national security minister publicly boasts of having worsened prison conditions for Palestinian security prisoners.

The Straits Times publishes an analysis of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's position on settler violence, noting he condemned the Qusra attack while continuing to back far-right coalition partners. No new strikes or casualties were reported in Gaza or Lebanon in the preceding 24 hours.

The UK Foreign Office says it has raised with Israeli authorities the detention of Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old British student activist forcibly detained by Israeli settlers in Umm al-Kheir in the occupied West Bank on Saturday before being arrested.

An Israeli strike killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza on Monday, health officials say: two killed and several wounded when a strike hit a crowd near the municipal public park in Gaza City, an area densely populated with displaced families, and at least three more killed later when a strike hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas militants in the first strike and did not immediately comment on the second. Casualty figures come from Gaza health officials.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Israel and Greece sign a EUR 3 billion (S$4.43 billion) agreement under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defence system for Greece, named "Achilles Shield", to be delivered by 2036. Israel's defence ministry confirmed the signing.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas announces that Yoav Segalovitz, a former Israeli police official and until recently a Yesh Atid member of the Knesset, will run on the moderate Islamist party's list in the 27 October election — the first Jewish Israeli to stand for an explicitly Arab party. Raam will campaign on an anti-crime platform. Segalovitz said there is “a difficult history between Arabs and Jews in this country, but there is also a shared future”.

An Israeli-backed raid to detain a Hamas figure in Gaza City is discovered mid-operation. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz says a senior Hamas member was captured, and an Israeli security official says the man detained heads Hamas's internal security service. Gaza officials and medics say air strikes launched to cover the force's withdrawal killed at least four people near the Katiba area of western Gaza City — two children and a woman among them — with another child killed in central Gaza; witnesses described at least 12 missiles fired into an area crowded with displaced families. Hamas government media office director Ismail al-Thawabta says the Israeli unit was detected before it could finish. Casualty figures come from Gaza medical sources and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Israeli defence ministry, Gaza medics, Hamas media office)

timeline.event: Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar warns Israel will retaliate if the UK imposes sanctions over the potential expansion of West Bank settlements. The warning came shortly after British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Parliament he would introduce a 'comprehensive reset' of policy on Israel in the coming weeks, including examining how to stop UK companies financing, constructing or advertising new settlements.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses security officials of deliberately failing to wake him on the morning of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, insisting the assault would have been contained had he intervened earlier - a day after his wife claimed an opposition figure knew of the attack in advance, prompting a threatened lawsuit. Netanyahu faces close-fought elections later in 2026. The 7 October attack killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 taken hostage; Gaza authorities report more than 73,000 Palestinians killed in the offensive that followed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli and Gaza authorities)

timeline.event: Unifil says the Israeli military has established four new bases in the areas of southern Lebanon it invaded, bringing the number of Israeli positions to nine, and reports consolidation and fortification of those positions along with demolition and engineering work. The strip under Israeli control is about 5 per cent of Lebanese territory and extends up to 10km from the border in places. A Lebanese intelligence official says Lebanon's military has recorded more than 5,000 violations of the June deal by Israel; the Israeli military says the buildings destroyed were used by Hezbollah for military purposes and that it acts in accordance with international law.
timeline.source: BBC (Unifil, Lebanese intelligence official, Israeli military)

timeline.event: More than 10 EU countries say they are willing to contribute to a planned European mission to train the Lebanese army.

Israel says a Hamas security chief was captured during a raid in Gaza City in which strikes killed four people, according to Gaza medics. Hezbollah's leader Naim Qassem last week called the US-brokered framework for the group's disarmament 'surrender with humiliation'.

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory so far in 2026 despite the ceasefire, taking the total since the 10 October truce past 1,300, including 301 children. The ministry does not separate civilians from combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable and BBC Verify says independent analysis is consistent with them; the Israeli military disputes the count, saying there is no basis to assume all those listed were killed by its activity, and says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire.

A BBC team travelling with Unifil inside the part of southern Lebanon under Israeli control reports entire villages flattened, with air strikes and demolitions continuing after the ceasefire announced in June. Lebanese officials say Israel is expanding its positions in the zone.

Two Palestinian teenagers are killed in an attack by Israeli settler militants and army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry say, amid an uptick in settler violence in the territory. Israel has not published its own account.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Palestinian health ministry, local officials)

timeline.event: The Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, named after a Shi'ite scholar whose shrine sits at its summit, has become one of the most contested pieces of ground in the Israel-Hezbollah war, according to a Straits Times explainer from Beirut.

Netanyahu visits Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip, his first trip there since the October 2025 ceasefire, and rejects mediators' push for a US-backed plan requiring withdrawal. 'We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line,' he says near the Yellow Line, adding that Israel controls 60 per cent of the strip. Hamas has not responded publicly to the visit.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's own Ebola count is running about 370 cases and 220 deaths ahead of WHO's last ratified figure, and it added 86 cases and 57 deaths in a single day — an epidemic still accelerating rather than levelling off. With Uganda's and France's monitoring windows closed it is now a single-country emergency, and responders have started using anonymised mobile-phone data to work out where the virus travels next. Europe's board is seasonal rather than alarming, though West Nile reached 25 newly affected areas in a single week. Closer to home, Singapore's flu wave is the one worth acting on — and if you are due a jab, US medical groups have just published fresh flu, Covid and RSV guidance.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Still a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; new confirmed cases now only in DR Congo
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cumulative figures as of 26 August, re-read this run from Disease Outbreak News 616 (published 28 August 15:28 UTC and still WHO's newest — the DON OData feed shows nothing after it): 5,794 cases in DR Congo (including two patients diagnosed there and later treated in Germany), 20 in Uganda and one in France, with 2,788 deaths including two in Uganda and at least 1,314 recovered. DR Congo's own national series, re-checked this run on ECDC's outbreak page (still last updated 2 September 16:08), is well ahead of that: 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths in the 1 September situation report covering data to 31 August, with 830 patients hospitalised in isolation and 1,409 recovered — a count WHO has not yet ratified in a DON. That report added 86 cases and 57 deaths in a single day, from Ituri (49), North Kivu (32) and Haut Uele (5); Ituri alone stands at 5,065 cases and 2,305 deaths, and 60 of 151 health zones are affected across six provinces. WHO declared Uganda's outbreak over on 25 August after 42 days without a new confirmed case, and DON 616 records the 42-day enhanced monitoring period as complete in both Uganda and France as of 27 August. Ervebo vaccination of health workers began in DR Congo on 27 August, though its protection against Bundibugyo virus in humans is unknown. This is the largest Ebola outbreak recorded in DR Congo and second only to the 2014-16 West African epidemic.

outbreaks.name: Global — cholera
outbreaks.status: Still spreading across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas; Nigeria dominates the current wave
outbreaks.scope_note: Worldwide totals since 1 January 2026, re-read again this run from ECDC's week-35 Communicable Disease Threats Report PDF (28 August, still the newest issued — the ECDC threats-report feed still shows no week 36 as of this run). Between 27 July and 26 August, 42,717 new cases and 257 new deaths were reported; Nigeria alone accounted for 41,296 cases and 242 deaths, followed by Angola (524), Somalia (489), Mozambique (319) and Chad (47). The country count is the 19 countries that reported new cases in that month. The previous reporting period (22 June to 27 July) had 8,247 new cases and 326 new deaths. For comparison, the same period of 2025 had run to 338,340 cases and 4,324 deaths. ECDC warns that case definitions, testing strategies and reporting completeness vary widely between countries, so the totals are an undercount.

outbreaks.name: United States — measles
outbreaks.status: Worst US year since elimination was declared in 2000; count still climbing
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC's confirmed 2026 count as of its 27 August data date, re-read from CDC's measles data page again this run and still the latest published figure: 2,887 cases reported by 47 jurisdictions plus 16 among international visitors, across 37 outbreaks, with 94% of confirmed cases (2,737 of 2,903) outbreak-associated. CDC's national total records no measles deaths; Pennsylvania separately reported two measles-associated deaths on 25 August that CDC says it is not including while it reviews whether measles caused or contributed to them.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission still expanding; 25 newly affected areas in a single week
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human cases in the 2026 season as at 26 August, from ECDC's weekly West Nile dashboard, which still shows week 35 (data to 26 August) as the latest published this run; the dashboard updates on Fridays, so the next refresh is due 4 September: Italy leads with 428, ahead of Greece on 222, Spain 79, North Macedonia 49, Romania 45 and France 28, with the remainder spread across nine more countries. The same report counts 124 affected areas across those 15 countries, 25 of them reported affected for the first time this season. The weekly dashboard is built for blood-donor deferral decisions and does not publish a season death count, hence the dash; ECDC's separate monthly report carried 12 deaths as of early August. National tallies can run ahead of ECDC's — Greek authorities reported 232 cases and 19 deaths as of 26 August, all deaths in patients over 65.

stories.headline: WHO and researchers turn to anonymised mobile-phone data to predict where Ebola spreads next
stories.summary: Health officials fighting the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in eastern DR Congo are using anonymised mobile-phone data to map population movements and identify areas where the virus could spread next, according to the World Health Organization and researchers working with it, The Straits Times reports. It is a targeting tool rather than a change in the case picture: WHO's last ratified count remains 5,815 confirmed cases and 2,788 deaths as of 26 August, while DR Congo's own 1 September report puts the national total at 6,186 cases and 3,007 deaths.
stories.source: The Straits Times (World Health Organization and partner researchers)

stories.headline: US medical groups issue their own Covid-19, flu and RSV vaccine guidance
stories.summary: Major US medical organisations released recommendations on Sep 2 for Covid-19, influenza and RSV vaccines, based on evidence reviews published in JAMA, saying they were filling a gap left by the Trump administration in "evidence-based vaccine guidance". They recommend updated Covid-19 shots for adults and at-risk young children, flu vaccination for everyone over six months, and RSV vaccines for older adults and pregnant women, plus monoclonal antibodies for infants at risk. The guidance lands as the US respiratory virus season begins and while the country runs its worst measles year since elimination.
stories.source: The Straits Times (US medical organisations, JAMA)

stories.headline: DR Congo's national count reaches 6,186 Ebola cases and 3,007 deaths, adding 86 cases in a day
stories.summary: DR Congo's 1 September situation report, carried on ECDC's outbreak page (last updated 2 September), puts the Bundibugyo virus epidemic at 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths with data to 31 August — an increase of 86 cases and 57 deaths on the previous day's report. The new cases came from Ituri (49), North Kivu (32) and Haut Uele (5); 830 patients are hospitalised in isolation, 1,409 have recovered, and 88 per cent of identified contacts are under follow-up. Ituri remains the worst-affected province at 5,065 cases and 2,305 deaths. These national figures run ahead of WHO's last ratified Disease Outbreak News count.

stories.headline: Indonesia tests government school meals after more than 500 students fall ill
stories.summary: More than 500 students in East Java's Sidoarjo region were hospitalised on Sep 1 with suspected food poisoning from state-supplied meals, deputy governor Emil Dardak said. Local government head Subandi said most of the 516 students treated had been discharged and that police had taken samples of the meals. The National Nutrition Agency, which runs President Prabowo Subianto's free-meals programme, is investigating whether the lunches were the cause. Watchdog Network for Education Watch counted some 37,600 food-poisoning cases linked to the programme as of 8 August.
stories.source: CNA (East Java officials, Network for Education Watch)

stories.headline: Influenza climbs in Singapore, with more than a third of community swabs testing positive
stories.summary: Singapore's Communicable Diseases Agency reported a jump in influenza cases, with more than a third of community swabs testing positive, but said there is no indication infections are more severe than usual. The agency's advice is unchanged and unglamorous: vaccination matters most for older adults and people with chronic conditions.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Communicable Diseases Agency)

stories.headline: WHO keeps the DR Congo Ebola emergency in place as confirmed cases reach 5,815
stories.summary: WHO's Disease Outbreak News 616, published 28 August and still its newest on this outbreak, records 5,815 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases as of 26 August — 5,794 in DR Congo, 20 in Uganda and one in France — with 2,788 deaths and at least 1,314 recoveries. The 42-day enhanced monitoring period closed in Uganda and France on 27 August, and WHO declared Uganda's outbreak over on 26 August, leaving new confirmed cases only in DR Congo. WHO says continuing intensity of transmission means the risk of cross-border exportation remains, and notes that Ervebo vaccination of health workers began on 27 August despite unknown protection against this virus species in humans.

stories.headline: Global cholera adds 42,717 cases in a month, four in five of them in Nigeria
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 Communicable Disease Threats Report records 42,717 new cholera cases and 257 new deaths worldwide between 27 July and 26 August, taking the 2026 total since 1 January to 212,857 cases and 1,943 deaths. Nigeria accounted for 41,296 of those new cases and 242 of the deaths, ahead of Angola, Somalia, Mozambique and Chad. The previous reporting month had recorded only 8,247 new cases, so the wave has sharply accelerated — though the 2026 running total is still well below the 338,340 cases reported by the same point in 2025.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35

stories.headline: Fatal diphtheria case in an unvaccinated four-year-old in Sicily
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 threats report leads with a fatal case of respiratory diphtheria in an unvaccinated child in Italy. Diphtheria is vaccine-preventable and rare in the EU, so a death is treated as a signal about vaccination coverage gaps rather than about the pathogen itself.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35

stories.headline: Second human swine-flu A(H1N2)v case linked to a Michigan county fair
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 threats report records a second human infection with swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v connected to a county fair in Michigan, citing US CDC. Variant influenza infections from pig contact at agricultural fairs are a recurring late-summer pattern in the US; the concern is sustained human-to-human transmission, which has not been reported here.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35 (US CDC)

stories.headline: West Nile virus reaches 877 human cases across 15 European countries
stories.summary: ECDC's weekly West Nile dashboard recorded 877 locally acquired human cases across 15 countries and 124 affected areas as of 26 August, with 25 areas reported affected for the first time this season. Italy leads on 428 cases, followed by Greece on 222 and Spain on 79. The weekly product is designed for blood-donor deferral decisions and does not publish a season death total; Greek authorities separately reported 232 national cases and 19 deaths, all in patients aged over 65.
stories.source: ECDC weekly West Nile virus surveillance dashboard, week 35

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: If you run a SonicWall SMA1000, patch it before reading the rest: two flaws the vendor says are already being exploited, one a pre-authentication SSRF scoring a perfect 10, sit on an internet-facing remote-access gateway. CISA added seven exploited bugs to its catalogue on Sep 2, and the ones most likely to be off your radar are a Kestra authentication bypass that also scores 10.0 and an authentication flaw in the LiteLLM AI gateway. That is the shape of this cycle: the AI stack is now ordinary attack surface, from Langflow being exploited to steal OpenAI and AWS keys to a booby-trapped .git config that can make coding agents run attacker code. Two quieter items are worth ten minutes each — Plex has emailed users to update without saying why, and attackers are staging a signed Node.js runtime so their payload never looks like a binary.

stories.headline: Phishing campaign in 46 countries installs legitimate remote-management tools, with the US the top target
stories.summary: A campaign running since January 2026 lures victims to a short-lived page hosted on a trusted cloud service or a compromised site, hands them an access code and a password-protected ZIP, and uses the Visual Basic script inside to make PowerShell fetch a legitimate remote monitoring and management installer — GoTo Resolve and LogMeIn Rescue in this arm, with ScreenConnect, ConnectWise and ITarian in related activity. Researchers recorded 425 kit URLs across 240 hosts between Feb 5 and Jul 29, with 94 per cent of hosts alive for a single day; about 45 per cent of activity is in the United States, and education, technology and government feature prominently. There is no patch here: alert on RMM agents your organisation does not deploy.

stories.headline: Plex emails users to update immediately, without saying what the flaws are
stories.summary: Plex has emailed users urging them to update, saying Plex Media Server 1.43.3 (released May 19) and Plex Desktop 1.115.0 (released Aug 13) address “a number of security issues” in earlier builds, BleepingComputer reports. Plex has published no technical detail and says CVEs have been requested but not yet issued; there is no report of exploitation. Media Server 1.43.2 and earlier are affected. Directly emailing users is an unusual step for the company, so treat this as higher priority than the missing detail suggests.

stories.headline: Attackers stage a signed Node.js runtime so their payload never looks like a binary
stories.summary: Instead of dropping a malicious executable, intruders install the legitimate, digitally signed Node.js runtime and use node.exe to run malicious JavaScript, keeping the logic in interpreted scripts that signature-based tools do not match; persistence comes from registering a node command that re-launches at every login. The Hacker News and Symantec's threat intelligence team report the technique in attacks since February 2026 against government departments, technology firms and hotels in Asia and the United States, in some cases alongside the ModeloRAT implant attributed to an initial access broker tracked as Woodgnat (also KongTuke), which has been linked to several ransomware operations. Hunt for node.exe running outside developer workflows.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Symantec threat intelligence

stories.headline: Shai-Hulud's credential-hunting reach keeps widening across npm and cloud secret stores
stories.summary: The self-spreading npm worm keeps expanding where it looks for secrets. The Hacker News reports its search now covers 469 distinct credential locations — a figure from that report alone, which we could not independently confirm. Published analyses of the campaign describe unified secret harvesting across AWS, GCP and Azure, reuse of GitHub tokens stolen from earlier victims so the worm survives a primary credential being revoked, and exfiltration into public GitHub repositories. Rotate every token a build agent has touched, not just the one you know leaked.
stories.source: The Hacker News (independent analyses of the Shai-Hulud campaign)

stories.headline: Citizen Lab confirms a Pegasus zero-click infection on a Serbian student activist's iPhone
stories.summary: Citizen Lab, working with Serbia's SHARE Foundation, says forensic artefacts from the iPhone of a member of Serbia's student protest movement show an iMessage zero-click exploit was used to install NSO Group's Pegasus, with high-confidence indicators of infection from December 2025 to January 2026. Apple patched the exploit chain in iOS 18.4.1. SHARE says 14 people were targeted in all, including a member of parliament and a local government official, and Amnesty International separately confirmed two devices infected with a new version of the NoviSpy spyware. NSO has said its tools are sold only to vetted government clients.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CyberScoop (Citizen Lab, SHARE Foundation, Amnesty International)

stories.headline: Researcher publishes a FalconFlank proof-of-concept claiming local privilege escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
stories.summary: A researcher going by Nightmare-Eclipse published FalconFlank, a public GitHub project with C source and a compiled x64 build that claims to escalate privileges locally by abusing CrowdStrike Falcon's remediation workflow for malicious Microsoft Office macros on Windows. The README says the issue affects devices with the "Microsoft Office file malicious macro removal" capability enabled, and that the proof-of-concept worked against fully patched Windows 11 25H2 and Windows Server 2025 with Phase 3 Optimal Protection. There is no CVE and no vendor confirmation - treat the "0day" label as an unverified researcher claim until CrowdStrike or independent analysis validates it. Defenders with Falcon deployed should watch for a vendor advisory.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Cyber Security News (researcher GitHub repository)

stories.headline: CISA adds seven actively exploited flaws to KEV, including a perfect-10 Kestra auth bypass
stories.summary: CISA's Sep 2 KEV update added seven vulnerabilities now confirmed as exploited, with attackers seen dropping reverse shells and crypto miners. Three are not otherwise in this briefing: an authentication-filter bypass in Kestra OSS (CVE-2026-49869, CVSS 10.0), where a path check using endsWith("/configs") lets unauthenticated requests through; improper authentication in the LiteLLM AI gateway's MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (CVE-2026-59822, CVSS 8.8), exploitable with a fabricated Authorization header; and HTTP request/response smuggling via an unvalidated Host header in Starlette (CVE-2026-48710, CVSS 6.5). The other four - JFrog Artifactory, Sangoma Switchvox and the two SonicWall SMA1000 flaws - are carded separately below. Federal agencies face KEV remediation deadlines; everyone else should treat these as patch-now.
stories.source: The Hacker News (CISA KEV catalog, NVD)

stories.headline: Attackers exploit critical Sangoma Switchvox SQL injection to drop reverse shells
stories.summary: An unauthenticated SQL injection in Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition 8.3 is being exploited to plant reverse shells on internet-facing PBX systems. Per NVD, the /pa endpoint processes XML beginning with <PolycomIPPhone> and concatenates a user-controlled value straight into a query; the flaw carries a CVSS v4 base score of 9.3 and was added to CISA's known-exploited catalogue on Sep 2. No credentials are needed, so exposed Switchvox systems should be patched or taken off the internet now.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News (CISA KEV, NVD)

stories.headline: SQL injection in All-in-One WP Migration leaves millions of WordPress sites exposed
stories.summary: A SQL injection in the archive-restore function of the All-in-One WP Migration and Backup plugin affects all versions up to and including 7.109, NVD records, with a CVSS v3.1 base score of 8.8. BleepingComputer reported that millions of installations remain unpatched and that the flaw can lead to site takeover. The CVE is not in CISA's known-exploited catalogue. Site owners should update the plugin immediately.

stories.headline: Fake software installers disable Windows Update and weaken Microsoft Defender
stories.summary: A campaign distributing trojanised software installers turns off Windows Update and weakens Microsoft Defender settings on infected machines before delivering its payload, The Hacker News reported. Disabling patching and downgrading endpoint protection keeps the host exploitable long after the initial infection, so unexpected changes to update or Defender policy are worth treating as an incident indicator.

stories.headline: Attackers mint admin tokens on JFrog Artifactory days after the fix shipped
stories.summary: An authentication weakness in JFrog Artifactory that, under default configuration, lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access obtain administrative privileges is being exploited within days of disclosure. NVD scores it 9.8 and CISA added it to the known-exploited catalogue on Sep 2. Artifactory sits at the centre of software build pipelines, so admin access there is a supply-chain foothold, not just a server compromise. Patch and rotate tokens.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News (CISA KEV, NVD)

stories.headline: Malicious .git configs can make Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents run attacker code
stories.summary: Researchers showed that a repository carrying a crafted .git configuration can cause AI coding agents - including Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex and Cursor - to execute attacker-controlled commands when the agent operates on the repo. No CVE has been assigned. The practical guidance is the old one, newly urgent: treat cloning an untrusted repository into an agent's working directory as running untrusted code, and sandbox agents that touch third-party source.

stories.headline: BGP hijack pushes a malicious Virtualizor update that plants persistent root access
stories.summary: Attackers hijacked BGP routes to intercept the update channel for Virtualizor, a virtualisation control panel, and served a malicious update that established persistent root access on servers that installed it. Poisoning the network path to a vendor's update endpoint defeats the usual trust in an in-product updater, so operators should verify package signatures out of band and audit Virtualizor hosts for unexpected root persistence.

stories.headline: Dropbox accounts taken over through a Lenovo ID email-verification flaw
stories.summary: BleepingComputer reported that Dropbox accounts were breached via a flaw in Lenovo's email verification, which let attackers assert control of addresses tied to Dropbox accounts and take them over. The chain is a reminder that a weakness in any identity provider a service will accept becomes a weakness in that service; Dropbox users who signed up or linked through a Lenovo ID should check active sessions and connected apps.

stories.headline: SonicWall SMA1000 zero-days chained for unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: SonicWall warned of two actively exploited SMA1000 flaws that researchers say may form an attack chain: a pre-authentication SSRF in the Appliance Work Place interface via an unintended alternate access path (CVE-2026-83548, CVSS 10.0), and post-authentication OS command injection in the Appliance Management Console (CVE-2026-83549, CVSS 7.8). Both were added to CISA's known-exploited catalogue on Sep 2. SMA1000 appliances are internet-facing remote-access gateways, so this is the highest-priority patch in this cycle.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer (SonicWall, CISA KEV, NVD)

stories.headline: GeoNetwork patches an unauthenticated RCE chain used in government geoportal backends
stories.summary: GeoNetwork, the open-source catalogue behind many government spatial-data portals, fixed a chain that researchers say allows unauthenticated remote code execution. The researchers assigned a CVSS of 8.6; neither CVE has an NVD record yet, so that score is researcher-assigned rather than authoritative, and the flaws are not in CISA's known-exploited catalogue. Agencies running GeoNetwork-backed geoportals should apply the OSGeo update.

stories.headline: Sality botnet infrastructure dismantled by turning its own peer-to-peer network against it
stories.summary: Authorities dismantled the distribution infrastructure of the long-running Sality botnet by using its own peer-to-peer protocol to cut infected hosts off from new malware payloads, in a joint global takedown. Sality has been used for years as a delivery layer for other malware, so the action removes a persistent loader from circulation - though infected machines remain infected and still need cleaning.

stories.headline: Researchers use Claude to port a pre-auth PLC exploit from one model to another
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated using Anthropic's Claude to adapt a pre-authentication remote code execution exploit written for one programmable logic controller so that it worked against a different model. The result is a data point on how far large language models compress the effort of porting industrial-control exploits across hardware - relevant to defenders sizing how quickly a single OT vulnerability can spread across a fleet of differing devices.

stories.headline: Attackers abuse the Faronics Deploy admin tool to install ScreenConnect
stories.summary: Attackers are abusing Faronics Deploy, a legitimate endpoint management tool, to push ScreenConnect remote-access software onto victim machines, BleepingComputer reported. Because both tools are signed, legitimate software, the activity blends into normal IT operations - detection has to come from watching for unexpected use of deployment tooling rather than from the binaries themselves.

stories.headline: Aesto Health says a breach exposed data on more than 9.5 million patients
stories.summary: Healthcare technology firm Aesto Health disclosed a data breach affecting more than 9.5 million patients, BleepingComputer reported. It is one of the larger health-sector exposures this cycle; affected individuals should expect notification and watch for targeted phishing that uses medical details as a lure.

stories.headline: Critical Langflow RCE exploited to steal OpenAI and AWS keys
stories.summary: A code-injection flaw in Langflow, the low-code framework for building LLM pipelines, is being exploited to run arbitrary code on affected installations and steal OpenAI and AWS credentials stored in them, BleepingComputer reported citing VulnCheck. NVD scores it 9.8. The CVE is not yet in CISA's known-exploited catalogue. Anyone running Langflow should patch and rotate every API key the instance held.

stories.headline: Thirteen malicious Packagist packages target unpatched iPhones to steal crypto wallet seeds
stories.summary: Thirteen malicious packages on Packagist, the PHP package registry, were built to target unpatched iPhones and steal cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases, The Hacker News reported. It is another instance of a language package registry being used as the delivery route for an attack aimed at end users rather than developers - dependency review and lockfile discipline are the defence.

stories.headline: Iranian operators pose as recruiters and deliver cross-platform RATs through coding tests
stories.summary: Iranian threat actors are posing as recruiters and using take-home coding assignments to deliver cross-platform remote access trojans to job-seeking developers, The Hacker News reported. The pattern mirrors North Korean fake-recruiter operations: the lure is a career opportunity, the payload runs when the candidate executes the supplied project. Developers should run any assessment code in a disposable VM.

stories.headline: Stolen METR API key burned roughly US$600,000 in AI credits
stories.summary: Attackers stole an API key belonging to the AI evaluations non-profit METR and consumed about US$600,000 worth of AI credits before it was cut off, The Hacker News reported. Leaked model-provider keys now carry direct, fast-accruing financial loss on top of data risk, which makes short-lived keys, spend caps and anomaly alerts on inference billing worth setting up before rather than after.

stories.headline: Russia-aligned UAC-0099 embeds a nuclear-weapon prompt in malware to derail AI analysis
stories.summary: The Russia-aligned group UAC-0099 planted text about nuclear weapons inside its malware in an apparent attempt to trip the safety filters of AI tools used to analyse samples, The Hacker News reported. It is an early example of adversaries writing prompt-injection and refusal-triggering content into payloads specifically to disrupt automated malware triage - worth accounting for by anyone routing samples through an LLM.
